question.leadin: China wasn't the only country that built great walls.
question.text: This Roman emperor built a namesake wall to mark the northern boundary of Roman Britain. He also suppressed the Bar Kokhba revolt in Judea.
question.clue: He twice avoided war with Parthia and he put down Bar Kokhba's Revolt, but he also defified his drowned lover, the Greek youth Antinous.

swap.leadin: This man was the first Roman emperor.
swap.text: Name this adopted son of Julius Caesar and member of the Second Triumvirate.
swap.clue: During his reign, the Pantheon was constructed on the commission of Marcus Agrippa.

question.leadin: This Master of the Horse under Julius Caesar and member of the Second Triumvirate went to Alexandria in 41 BCE.
question.text: Name this Roman general and politician, the lover of Cleopatra.
question.clue: Cicero's head and hands were sent to this leader after Cicero attacked him in his writings and this man was defeated at the Battle of Actium.

swap.text: The loss at Cannae triggered a change in Roman strategy, leading to final victory in this war at the Battle of Zama.
swap.clue: Quintus Fabius Maximus Cunctator , the "Delayer," gained his name by advocating a policy of attrition in this conflict.

question.text: In 8 B.C. Augustus assumed this office whose duties included overseeing the counting of the people. This official could also remove names from the senator list; overseeing publications is an act such officials still do today.
question.clue: Only former consuls could be named to this powerful office, which determined eligibility for voting and oversaw public morals laws.

swap.text: The Capitoline Hill is at one end of this general area of Rome, where most of the politics of the day took place. The arch of Titus leads into this area, which contains the temple of Diana.
swap.clue: This place replaced the Comitium and was the site of the Basilica Aemilia.The Arch of Titus is located on the Via Sacra southeast of this place that is located between the Palatine and Capitoline Hills.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of Rome.
question.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
question.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors and their roles in the Crisis of the Third Century.
swap.text: This emperor, dubbed "Restitutor Orbis" for his conquest of Zenobia's Palmyrene Empire in 273 and the Gallic Empire in 274, helped end the Crisis of the Third Century.
swap.clue: At the Battle of Immae ("IM-mye"), this emperor's generals exploited the desert to tire the cataphracts of the general Zabdas.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Emperor Augustus's religious reforms.
question.text: Suetonius (sweh-TOH-nee-uss) notes that Augustus revived this February festival, whose celebrants sacrifice goats, then don strips of the goatskin while running a circuit around the Palatine Hill that started and ended in a cave.
question.clue: This event originated when King Amulius ordered two men to be thrown into the Tiber River as punishment.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people who may have come from Lydia or Umbria.
swap.text: This Italian civilization, which was eventually absorbed by the Romans, had no centralized government. Instead, it was comprised of a loose Confederation of cities like Clusium and Veii.
swap.clue: The names of gods in this language are on a sheep liver-shaped bronze artifact used for haruspicy found at Piacenza.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Roman occupation of Britain.
question.text: As governor of Britannia, this Roman general subdued the Caledonians and Ordovices, winning the battle of Mons Graupius in Scotland. Father-in-law of Tacitus, he was recalled by Domitian, but not before he circumnavigated Britain.
question.clue: He served under Salvius Titianus after being appointed quaestor in Asia and after he shared a battle tent with his military tutor Suetonius Paulinus.

swap.text: This emperor retired to his palace in Croatia in 305. He is best known for creating the tetrarchy and for a persecution of Christians.
swap.clue: After disposing of his rival Carinus, he established Sirmium, Trier, Milan and Nicomedia as subsidiary capitals.

question.text: Gnaeus Plancius's rape of a mima was defended by this Roman orator, who also exposed the Catiline Conspiracy.
question.clue: This man asked when a senator would "cease abusing our patience" after a 63 BC plot.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the evolution of imperial offices in the late Roman Empire.
swap.text: A group of elite scholae ("SKOH-lye") who served as imperial guards were named for this geographic feature in Rome where emperors lived. Before the imperial era, this place mainly housed the homes of the wealthy.
swap.answerHtml: Palatine Hill [accept Scholae Palatinae; prompt on palace by saying "we're looking for a geographic feature"]
swap.clue: Dionysius of Halicarnassus places the home of one individual near the Scalae Caci on the south side of this location.

question.leadin: Answer the following about attacks on Roman control in Hispania.
question.text: This former shepherd and leader of the Lusitani rose up against Roman control after a governor dug a trench around a group of Lusitani and killed them while they were surrendering their weapons. This leader defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Mt. Veneris.
question.clue: Polybius called the long struggle with this leader of the Lusitanians the "War of Fire" for its violence. Wildly successful against Rome on the battlefield, he was killed in his sleep by three bribed Tartessian assassins.

swap.leadin: In a poem describing God, he wrote that God "is indescribable" even to Jesus.
swap.text: Name this author of "Thalia" whose views were criticized by Athanasius (ath-uh-NAY-shus) in On the Councils of Ariminum and Seleucia (uh-RIM-in-um and si-LOO-shuh)
swap.clue: While speaking at an event, this person was apocryphally slapped by an outraged man from Patara.

question.text: This confederate of the lawyer Celestius wrote the tract On Free Will but was condemned by Pope Zosimus at the Council of Carthage for his belief in the ability of men to save themselves.
question.clue: This British heretic, who famously denied original sin and incurred the wrath of St. Augustine.

swap.text: Name this class of gladiator that usually fought against the Hoplomachus or the Thraex; the similar Secutor was usually instead paired against the Retiarius [reh-tee-AR-ee-us].

question.leadin: Two thousand years ago, the proudest boast was "civis romanus sum"-or "I am a Roman citizen." Unfortunately, not everyone could make that boast.
question.text: Name this status of people, especially barbarian tribes, who served Rome as mercenaries and received some privileges but were not conferred any of the benefits of Roman citizenship. Goths with this status were essential in defeating the Huns.

swap.text: The bronze hand likely survived because it was in a village burned down by the Romans in a war against this general, who led Iberian tribes in a 1st-century BCE revolt against Rome after he was proscribed by Sulla.
swap.clue: Along with his lieutenant Hirtuleius, he overthrew the governor Quintus Metellus Pius, and then was joined by Marcus Perpenna, though Perpenna eventually had this man murdered at a banquet.
